The three primitives form a coherent mathematical foundation for probabilistic sports intelligence. Conformal prediction ensures calibrated uncertainty bounds, which is essential for risk-sensitive betting strategies. Empirical Bayes shrinkage stabilizes estimates in low-data regimes, particularly useful for emerging players or teams. The Hawkes process enables modeling of event clustering and temporal dynamics—critical for simulating realistic game sequences. Together, they support both static inference (GSI) and dynamic reasoning (GSE), forming a robust dual-layer architecture. Failure modes include over-reliance on exchangeability assumptions in conformal methods, poor generalization in shrinkage when priors mismatch reality, and mis-specification of excitation kernels in Hawkes models.
